newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended strong on Friday boosted by bullish U.S. unemployment data which lifted industrials in the afternoon after a weaker start.
Golds ended at yet another fresh four-year low on a lacklustre bullion price which failed to break above the $340 an ounce level.
"The market opened softly on a weaker Dow last night but the good payroll figure lifted shares," a dealer said.

U.S. Labour Department data showed non-farm payrolls rose 142,000 in the month, compared with analysts expectations of a 211,000 fuelling hopes that a rate rise in the United States would be off the cards for a while.
Institutions were conspicous by their absence after the Workers Day public and market holiday on Thursday and as many players had taken Friday off to make a long weekend.
Volumes traded were light compared to the record volumes seen last Friday and on Tuesday.
Gold counters were mostly mixed with little activity as players watched the dull bullion price.

"I still think that we will see more downside on gold shares because the reality of a stronger rand and a weaker bullion price has started to sink in," said Willi Jonker, executive director of portfolio management at Norwich Investments.
The industrial index ended up 44.2 points at 8,538.5, the all-share index gained 18.5 points to 7,149.0 points and the gold index lost 5.4 points to 1,181.6 points.
Shares in Powertech jumped 8.5 percent to 8.25 rand in volume of 40,100 shares ahead of the release of its annual earnings on Friday.

Analysts had expected a rise of eighteen percent in profits, although they said pinning an actual figure earnings figure was difficult as last year's data could be restated to take account of the sale of its General Technologies unit.
Randgold gained 225 cents to 30.25 rand or over eight percent after recovering some of Wednesday's losses due to a weak bullion price.
Metcash was down 30 cents to 400 cents after it was pushed up to 430 cents on Wednesday. Dealers said the stock was at fair value at 400 cents.
Conshu traded four cents lower at 160 cents after reporting weak year results on Friday. Dealers said the clothing sector has generally been hard hit by imports.
Sea Harvest was up 30 cents to 450 cents on strong interim results which saw headline earnings per share up 21 percent.
Near-term industrial share futures were firmer, helped by the bullish U.S. unemployment figure. Golds were steady on a lacklustre bullion price.
Dealers said many players had taken Friday off and trade was quiet with light volumes traded.
The June all-share contract was at 6,660/70 from 6,623, the industrial contract was at 8,390/95 from 8,330 and the gold contract was at 830/50 from 836.
